name: Kansas

office.name: Kansas Department of Transportation - Central Permitting Office (K-TRIPS)

fees.note: Standard single-trip permit $40 (K.S.A. 8-1911(f)(2)(A)); one permit covers oversize and overweight. Only the highest line in this group is charged.
Large structure single trip $200: over 16'6" wide (K.A.R. 36-45-1 definition).
Large structure single trip $200: over 18' high.
KDOT's 2025 presentation also lists length over 126' as a large structure ($200); K.A.R. 36-45-1 defines large structure by width/height only - verify.
Superload single trip $200: over 150,000 lb gross (K.A.R. 36-45-1). A load is also a superload if any axle group exceeds K.A.R. 36-1-37 limits even under 150,000 lb (not modeled).

restrictions.text: Over-width or over-length permitted loads may not travel from 30 minutes after sunset to 30 minutes before sunrise (unless authorized by another statute/regulation), when visibility is under 1/2 mile, or when the highway has ice, snow pack or drifting snow.
Overweight-only permitted loads (legal width and length) may operate 24 hours a day, except when highway surfaces have ice, snow pack or drifting snow.
KHP: oversize and overweight loads may not move when visibility is under 1/2 mile or in moderate to heavy rain, sleet, snow, fog or smoke, or on slippery roads (K.A.R. 36-1-36).

Urban curfews may apply 7-9 a.m. and 4-6:30 p.m. in Kansas City, Lawrence, Leavenworth, Leawood, Lenexa, Olathe, Overland Park, Shawnee, Topeka and Wichita (pickups/deliveries in those cities excluded) - check the permit.

notes: Escorts (K.A.R. 36-45-8): over 14' wide = front and rear escort, but the rear escort may be dropped if a warning light is on top of the load, another on the rear of the load 2'-8' above the road, and a rear warning sign - modeled as front only. Large structures (over 16'6" wide or 18' high) and superloads need front and rear; a superload that must slow at bridges needs one more. Kansas sets no length-based escort rule in K.A.R. 36-45.

Every escorted move: an escort operator must survey the permitted route within 14 days before the move (K.A.R. 36-45-7(b)). Over 16' high, the lead escort must carry a height pole. Escort operators must be certified and the provider registered with KDOT. KHP does not provide escorts.
The escort regulation PDF posted on K-TRIPS shows blank effective dates (temporary-regulation copy); confirm the adopted text in the Kansas Administrative Regulations.
Holiday/weekend travel restrictions were not found in the sources fetched (K.A.R. 36-1 not reachable) - verify with KDOT.
Permit is valid only if the power unit is registered for at least the gross weight (K.S.A. 8-1911(c)).

Legal: 8'6" wide (K.S.A. 8-1902), 14' high, semitrailer 59'6"; K.S.A. 8-1904(c) caps most combinations at 65' overall, but federal law bars overall-length caps for tractor-semitrailers on the National Network - modeled as no overall limit. Gross 80,000 lb on interstates; the bridge table allows up to 85,500 lb on other state highways.
